title: The king under the lake
hookLine: the last Kaurava king walks into a lake, and some hunters overhear
carry: sakshi: every deed has a witness
tomorrow: the hidden king makes an offer. should they take it?

cards: One man walks away from the battlefield on foot, carrying a mace. His horse is dead. His army is gone.
His brothers, his friends, his commanders have fallen. He is the king the whole war was fought for, and he is alone.

On the way he meets Sanjaya, his father's companion, and gives him a message for the blind old king at home: tell my father I've gone into the lake. Then Duryodhana walks down to the water's edge, and keeps walking.

teach.b: In Ganguli's English, Duryodhana enters the lake and, by a power of illusion he knows, binds the waters around him so he can rest beneath them, hidden.
The lake lies smooth and still, and the last Kaurava king lies under it. Three survivors of his army find the lake: Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. They call down: come out, fight with us.
From under the water he answers: not tonight. I'm wounded and tired.
Then some hunters pass, men who bring meat to Bhima's kitchen. They hear a king talking from under a lake, and they know the Pandavas are searching for him, so they go and tell Bhima.
The Pandavas come with Krishna, and Yudhishthira calls to the still water: why are you hiding? Duryodhana answers from below: I'm not afraid. I'm only resting.
Here's the teaching. Much earlier in this same epic, Shakuntala tells a king who pretends not to know her: you think you alone know what you did.
But the sun and moon, wind and fire, earth, sky and water, your own heart, day and night, and dharma itself witness what a person does.
Hindus call that witness sakshi. It's why a Hindu wedding vow is made with Agni, the fire, as witness. Duryodhana hid in the one place he thought no one could see, and the water was a witness too.
The lake kept his body. It couldn't keep his secret.

how: Duryodhana's hiding in the lake, told in the Shalya Parva, is retold in readings, regional theater and serials of the Mahabharata, and the lake scene leads into the war's final duel.

s: Duryodhana fled the field on horseback with his guard
his horse was dead, his army gone; he walked away alone with his mace.
some hunters who brought meat to Bhima gave away the hiding place
they overheard the king talking from under the water.
in the epic, a deed done where no one sees has no witness
Shakuntala names the witnesses: sun, moon, wind, fire, earth, sky, water, the heart and dharma.

games.q: at a Hindu wedding, the couple makes their vows around a sacred fire. by today's teaching, why the fire?
o: Agni is the sakshi, the witness, so the vow is seen.
the fire is only there for light and warmth.
it burns away the past so nothing before counts.
games.why: Hindus speak of a vow made with Agni as sakshi, witness. like the water over Duryodhana, the fire sees what's done.

practice: Let your body grow still, the way a lake does when the wind drops. Bring to mind something you do when you think no one's watching, kind or not so kind. Hindus say God dwells in every heart as the inner witness.
If you pray, offer it there, in your own words. If you don't pray, picture it in plain daylight, and ask whether you'd still choose it.

wordCard.voice: Shalya. The book of the war's last day: the commander fallen, and Duryodhana lying hidden under a lake until hunters give him away.

orig.note: Duryodhana: the eldest Kaurava, hidden under the lake.
